# tsk

> tsk is a terminal task board for you and your agents: one shared queue, a TUI for you, a CLI for them.

On macOS/Linux, install with `curl -fsSL https://gettsk.sh/install.sh | sh` or `brew install smarzban/tap/tsk`. On Windows 10/11 ARM64 or x86-64, run `irm https://www.gettsk.sh/install.ps1 | iex` in a PowerShell window (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7); it selects the native architecture. Download the script first to use `-NoPathUpdate`, which leaves user PATH unchanged. Windows package-manager submissions and signing are not included yet.
If Herdr is on PATH, the installer asks to run `tsk setup herdr` on an interactive terminal; when agent skill roots are detected it also asks once to install the tsk skill. The install ends with a single `Done.` line pointing at the board (plus the Herdr board shortcut after an accepted Herdr setup) and one row per skipped ask (`tsk setup herdr`, `tsk setup`); a custom `TSK_INSTALL_DIR` skips the asks and says so. Homebrew prints the Herdr setup command as a caveat.
Herdr's board shortcut opens or focuses one board per workspace across its tabs, preserving its view and edits. Other workspaces stay untouched; boards share the same task store.
Details: https://gettsk.sh/docs/install.md
Inside Git, the board opens the repo root's project. Outside Git, it opens the `all` scope. The scope picker (`p`) chooses `all`, `desk`, or one project; quick-add from `all` or `desk` goes to the desk, and from a project board to that project. In `!p name`, `tsk add -p name`, and JSON plans, a bare project name must uniquely match a known project; a new project destination requires an existing absolute directory (`/…` or `~/…` on macOS/Linux, `C:\…` or `~\…` on Windows).
On the task page or the wide detail, `P` opens a parent picker (type to filter, Enter saves, Escape closes) and `U` clears the parent. Both act on the open task only, refuse while a draft has unsaved changes, and never change either task's status, scope, or children. The page shows the parent line before the steps (`not found · link kept` for a deleted or missing parent, whose UUID stays) and the direct children with a done count after them; board rows with children end in a dim `⊂done/total` count. Tab and arrows select the parent and child lines; Enter or a click opens that task without changing the list, Escape returns to the previous task, and Enter on `parent  none` opens the picker. Long picker titles wrap.
New tasks start with status `todo`. The board shows Doing, then Todo, in task-number order (`S` groups them by project). Use `tsk list --todo` or `--doing` to filter. Task status is only `todo`, `doing`, or `done`; questions and Herdr execution status are separate. The board checks GitHub releases at most daily and shows a dim `vX.Y.Z available, run tsk update` on the status row; set `TSK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` to disable. Run `tsk update` to run the official installer for an installer-managed copy; on Windows a detached helper waits for the running executable to exit before replacing it. Existing Herdr registration and outdated installed agent skills are refreshed; when no agent skill is installed, an interactive update can offer the first-install skill setup. Homebrew copies print `brew update && brew upgrade tsk` instead.
Store format v8 removes the Task thread label from live and trashed tasks; v7 mapped `open`/`ready` to `todo`, `started`/`blocked`/`review` to `doing`, and kept `done`. Earlier migrations still run in order, including v5 batch undo and v6 optional parent_task_id UUID relationships. Migration keeps a `tsk.json.vN` original-version backup; trash gets an original-byte `trash.jsonl.pre-v8` backup before its first rewrite. History, undo, revisions, archive flags, steps, parents, and question references are preserved. `--thread`, list thread filters, the JSON `thread` field, and quick-add `!t` are gone; a non-null plan `thread` is an `invalid-item` refusal. Name a working Thread with a `Thread: <agent-name> <workspace-id> <tab-id> <pane-id>` notes line instead. Restore matched live/trash backups together for rollback; older binaries refuse the newer store.
`N` tasks on the desk are human-only notices: four starter tasks on a first open, one `What's new in tsk` task after an upgrade. `tsk list` never shows them.
Press Shift+M to enter multi-select, then mark tasks with Space, shifted arrow keys, or a plain click and use the board's status, archive, or delete shortcut on the whole set. Shift+M again while the board owns input, an action, Escape, or a scope change exits the mode and clears its session-only marks; removing the last mark alone keeps the mode active, and text entry keeps Shift+M as a capital M. Enter and edit remain cursor-only. Board rows show the number and title only, in task-number order, then a bold `!` (an approval waiting on you) or `?n` (questions and findings waiting on you); `S` toggles a project grouping (session-only, never a task change). The CLI keeps its own order. At 110 usable columns or wider, the board is always a list beside the selected task's detail: right arrow, l, or Enter focuses the detail, left arrow, h, or Escape returns to the list, and clicking a task updates the detail with list focus. On the detail or a task page, `J`/`K` opens the next or previous task in list order; a dirty draft refuses. Text entry keeps h and l as characters.

Press `/` to filter the rows the board shows. Every whitespace-separated query term must match the title, notes, steps, or `T` number. `Enter` pins the query and returns input to board keys, while `Esc` clears the input or a pinned query first. Done rows show only while the done drawer is open; the closed DONE heading keeps the count of matching done tasks. Changing scope clears search.

The quit shortcut exits from non-editor board surfaces, including task pages, Help, and pickers. Text entry keeps its editing behavior; save recovery must be resolved first. Unsaved drafts block quitting, including a draft parked in the detail column. Quit attempts preserve the pending save's failure message. Escape dismisses editors and overlays first, then returns detail focus to the list; task drafts stay parked. Escape then quits without confirmation at the list root on any scope, never switching scope first. The browser demo releases keyboard focus at root instead of exiting. See the Keys guide for shortcuts.

On an explicit Agent board, `2` opens the questions tab: NEEDS APPROVAL, FOR YOU, FINDINGS, WITH LEAD, and CLOSED, with records without an audience shown apart as target unknown and left out of the tab number and row marks. `Enter` opens a record (side by side at 110+ columns); `j`/`k` and `Enter` answer, `Space` checks an approval's exact target, scope, and revision before `y` approves (`n` rejects), `c` corrects, `t` opens the task, `r` resends a lead request, `J`/`K` step, `PgUp`/`PgDn` or the wheel scroll the page. A saved answer returns to the list with the cursor on the next waiting record; CLOSED is folded until `z`. Clicks follow the keys: an option click chooses without saving, the check line checks, and a page line or footer entry naming a key acts as that key. A finding offers create-and-run (a Doing task plus an identifier-only request to its `lead_recipient` when exactly one live agent has that name), create-only, or close, never creating a second task and never creating one in an archived project. Quitting is refused while an answer is typed or a question save is unresolved. The board shows `waiting on you  approval n · question n · finding n  → 2` when something waits, plus `target unknown n`. The task page lists the task's questions, findings, and `Linear:`/`PR:`/`CI:`/`Thread:` notes lines; a Thread line focuses a pane only on an exact single four-token live match. On the task page, bare `e` edits and bare `a` adds a step.

`tsk threads` opens a read-only Herdr view of live lead and issue-thread sessions, grouped only by Herdr execution status: BLOCKED, IN MOTION, ON DECK. It never reads or writes the task or question store. Inbox metadata is optional annotation only; it does not change grouping or indicate a wait for the user. See the Threads guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/threads.md

## For agents

- `tsk guide` prints the workflow; `tsk setup` detects agents and can install the skill; `tsk setup <agent>` targets one agent
- The skill covers rules of engagement, board language, the exit contract, and workflows, and points at `tsk help <command>` for syntax; its `Refine a task` section shapes a rough task into a brief on the board (propose, then write)
- `tsk list T<n>` returns the complete task, including notes and steps, in human-readable or JSON form
- `tsk steps T<n> move <short-id> --before|--after <short-id>` (or `--first`/`--last`) reorders a step, keeping its short ID and checked state; `tsk steps T<n> add "…"` takes the same place flags. On the task page, a keyboard shortcut moves the selected step and adding a step with one selected puts it directly below
- `tsk list` groups Doing before Todo and orders Todo oldest capture first; Doing and Done use most recent status change first. This is separate from the board's number order. `--json` is that flat board order; with `--all`, human output groups each status by scope, ordering the groups by their first row and keeping the board order inside each group
- `tsk import linear` (needs `LINEAR_API_KEY`) creates a task per Linear issue, one way: title `<IDENTIFIER> <title>`, notes starting `Linear: <IDENTIFIER> <url>`, which also dedupes reruns. Filters `--team`, `--linear-project`, `--assignee`, `--state`, `--limit`; destination `-p` or `--desk`; `--update` refreshes title and status of existing copies; `--dry-run` writes nothing; `--json` prints a report. Missing key or Linear errors exit 1 with nothing saved. macOS and Linux only
- `tsk add --parent T10` and JSON plan `parent` strings select one parent; `tsk edit T12 --parent T10` replaces it, `--no-parent` clears it. Self/cycles refuse. `tsk list T10 --json` includes direct parent/children and calculated Done/total counts; archived children count, deleted children/notices do not. Deleted/missing parents retain their UUID as unresolved; no state changes cascade.
- Linear import reads only the direct parent identifier/URL, keeps `Parent: Linear <identifier> <URL>` in new-task Notes, and links an existing or same-batch imported parent by UUID. No recursive import or later reconciliation. `--update` keeps user Notes and parent relation. External GitHub Notes use `Parent: GitHub <repo>#<num> <URL>`; GitHub intake is separate.
- `tsk ask --file question.json`, `tsk questions [Q-number|UUID] [--task T<n>]`, `tsk answer Q1 --file answer.json`, and `tsk route Q1 --file route.json` (set `audience` `user`/`lead` and `lead_recipient` under the same Q number, given `expected_revision`) require an explicitly selected non-personal Agent state directory (`--state-dir` or `TSK_STATE_DIR`). They never fall back to the personal board. Questions preserve full text, Task/Q UUID separation, expected-revision CAS and append-only corrections. Shared `tsk.json` holds only shareable summaries/references; private question and approval originals stay in Git-excluded `questions-private/`. Answers persist before identifier-only Herdr notification; registration targets recipient and answers/corrections target origin Thread. Saved, notification failed, and durability uncertain are separate outcomes. Ordinary Agent/imported answers never issue user approval. Confirmed UI or verified original user-chat evidence binds approval to exact target/action/H-or-plan-digest/scope/rollback. No PIN, ACL, chmod protection, encryption or signature is added; same-OS-account UI impersonation is not prevented. CLI refuses UserUi origin. Full JSON and retry rules: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- Guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/agents.md
- CLI: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- `tsk help [<command>]` prints the CLI or one command's syntax reference.
- `tsk --version` (or `tsk -V`) prints the installed version.

Storage, backups, and release-check settings: https://gettsk.sh/docs/storage.md
- Full docs: https://gettsk.sh/llms-full.txt
